controls_for_engineering_rules.rule: A MUTATION BATTERY FIRES PER SITE, NEVER PER SYMBOL-OWNER, AND A KILLED TALLY NAMES ITS DENOMINATOR'S UNIT.
controls_for_engineering_rules.statement: When one class, module or function owns MORE THAN ONE instance of the construct under test, a mutant applied per owner is killed by whichever instance the arms happen to observe and says NOTHING about its siblings. The tally is then arithmetically true and false as a coverage claim.
controls_for_engineering_rules.measured: Inc-5's round-3 battery fired per renderer CLASS and reported '18 fired / 18 KILLED'. There are SEVEN hit sites across SIX classes: RailTimelineRenderer holds two (lane.py:228 trunk, lane.py:291 label). Demonstrated directly: MAX at the trunk site alone = KILLED; MAX at the label site alone = SURVIVED; MAX at BOTH sites as one per-class mutant = KILLED -- reporting a kill over a live survivor. The round-4 per-site battery found it: 35 fired across 7 sites x 5 shapes, 32 KILLED, 3 proven equivalent by output digest.
controls_for_engineering_rules.discharge: State the battery's denominator in its own units ('7 sites', not '6 renderers'), enumerate the sites, and fire one mutant per site. A survivor is a finding unless proven EQUIVALENT by output digest over an enumerated input set, with a positive control that must differ.

controls_for_engineering_rules.origin: Inc-5, measured across FOUR independent review rounds, each of which blocked on the same defect one quantifier further out.
controls_for_engineering_rules.rule: ANYTHING SPELLED TWICE WILL DRIFT. DERIVE IT -- AND AUDIT THE DECLARATION OF DERIVATION AGAINST THE CODE THAT DOES IT, BECAUSE THE COMMENT SAYING "DERIVED" IS ITSELF A SPELLING.
controls_for_engineering_rules.statement: An oracle's blind spots migrate outward one quantifier at a time. Fixing the instance a reviewer named is necessary and never sufficient: each correct fix relocates the blind spot to the next enclosing quantifier, so a review that checks only the assertion keeps passing an oracle whose guarantee is exactly as wide as whatever its author last remembered to name. AND THE LAST RUNG IS THE DECLARATION ITSELF -- a comment, a docstring or a gate checkbox asserting 'derived' is a second spelling of the claim, and it drifts from the code exactly like any other duplicate.
controls_for_engineering_rules.measured: Six generations across two increments and six independent review rounds. ZERO defects in shipped behaviour were found in any round; every block was the oracle or its declaration.
controls_for_engineering_rules.discharge: Derive the thing from the artifact that owns it rather than naming it, and ASSERT the boundary that justifies any exclusion -- a bare derivation silently ABSORBS the defect, since anything the code stops producing simply leaves the derived set. Then audit the DECLARATION against the code: read every comment, docstring and checked gate box that claims a property, and confirm the code has it. On the sixth exhibit the false declaration sat seven lines from the true one and no test could see it -- only a reader comparing the two.
exhibits: 1 MEMBER -- the assertion named `min`; its mirror `max` survived at 7 of 7 renderers.
2 LIST -- the assertion named its members while the BATTERY fired per CLASS; a per-class mutant reported a KILL over a live survivor at a sibling site.
3 CARDINALITY -- the assertion drove one pair of size 2; MINMAX/SORTED2 (drop a MIDDLE member) survived 7/7, and no hit set of size >= 3 existed anywhere in the repository.

4 DOMAIN -- the assertion quantified correctly over a hand-named domain; a drop-root mutant survived all 50 arms AND the entire 904-arm default lane at 3 of 7 sites, with root operator-reachable via SearchIndex.hits('raiz').

5 WIDTH -- the domain was correctly derived, but derived at ONE width (120) while the siblings backstopping two of its four members run at 80; a width-conditioned drop of either was absorbed by the derivation and unseen by the backstops.

6 MEMBERSHIP, AND IT IS THE DECLARATION EXHIBIT -- the titles were derived and the DOMAIN's own membership was left spelled, seven lines under a comment reading 'THE DOMAIN AND THE TITLES BOTH COME FROM THE FIXTURE, spelled nowhere', in an increment titled 'the last hand-spelled thing removed', under a gate box checked [x] for that property. A RENAME in the fixture is loud (KeyError); an ADDITION is SILENT -- a fifth node stays outside the domain, the boundary and the unions.

controls_for_engineering_rules.rule: A GAP ROUTED TO THE WRONG OWNER IS A GAP BEHIND A CLOSED DOOR.
controls_for_engineering_rules.statement: Filing a live gap under an existing carry closes it to review: the carry is already known, already accepted and already owned, so nobody re-examines whether it actually covers the case filed under it. A mis-route is more dangerous than an unfiled gap, because an unfiled gap still looks open.
controls_for_engineering_rules.measured: Inc-5's oracle excluded the map root from its domain and justified the exclusion by citing carry B-55 ('a clipped hit is an undeclared hit'). B-55 is TRUE of the three lane renderers, which iterate branches and never draw the root. It is INAPPLICABLE to outline, radial and layered, which draw the root AND paint it as a hit (measured 1, 13 and 20 hit-styled spans) -- and those three are the operator-reachable renderers. A drop-root defect there was invisible to the whole suite while appearing, in the artifact, to be an accepted carry. The root is reachable from an ordinary search: SearchIndex.hits('raiz') returns it.
controls_for_engineering_rules.discharge: Before routing a gap to an existing carry, check the carry's scope against the SPECIFIC case being routed, per member of the affected population rather than per family. Where the justification is a property of the artifact ('this renderer does not draw that node'), assert it FROM the artifact rather than citing the carry.

The suspension notice is the load-bearing half: declaring the count without it trades one hidden state for another. (2) esc clears in ALL regimes.
